("Vesicor" or the "Company"), an early development stage biotechnology company focused on the development of p53-based cancer therapeutics delivered via precision-engineered microvesicles, announced the closing of its previously announced business combination with Black Hawk Acquisition Corporation ( VESI ) ("Black Hawk"). The transaction was approved by Black Hawk's shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting held on October 13, 2026 and closed on November 19, 2026. In connection with the closing, Black Hawk domesticated from the Cayman Islands to Delaware and changed its name to Vesicor Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. The Company's common stock is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker symbol "VESI" on November 23, 2026.

Vesicor will be led by Michael Tolentino, MD, Chief Executive Officer; Luo Feng, PhD, Founder, Director and Chief Scientific Officer; Mitch Creem, MHA, Chief Financial Officer; and Warren Hosseinion, Jr., Chief Operating Officer. data.title: Arrvel's New Panel PC Series: Fanless Industrial PCs Built for Harsh Edge Environments
data.description:
SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Industrial edge computing is facing a reliability crisis. As manufacturers, power utilities, and commercial operators push digitization deeper onto the factory floor and into unattended field environments, the hardware tasked with running MES terminals, SCADA front-ends, and self-service kiosks is routinely failing under conditions it was never designed to survive. Sustained vibration, metal particulate infiltration, electromagnetic interference, and wide temperature swings continue to expose the fragility of consumer-grade tablets and commercial PCs in 24/7 operational settings. Today, Arrvel is addressing that gap with the launch of its industrial panel pc series—a family of integrated panel pc solutions that combine industrial-grade displays, projected capacitive touchscreens, embedded processing, and extensive control interfaces inside a fanless, fully sealed aluminum chassis. Unlike standard commercial PCs, these industrial PCs are engineered specifically for continuous industrial duty.

Industrial Touch Panel PC Engineering for Continuous Operation

The Arrvel industrial touch panel pc lineup is built around a unified thermal, mechanical, and electrical architecture that prioritizes longevity over aesthetics. The chassis employs a CNC-machined front bezel paired with a one-piece extruded-aluminum rear heat sink. The anodized oxidation surface treatment increases thermal radiation efficiency, while the fin structure expands surface area by a factor of three to five—enough to dissipate heat from sustained CPU loads without any moving parts. Environmental hardening extends beyond thermal management. The front panel carries an IP65 ingress protection rating, sealing against dust and low-pressure water jets. The hardware platform operates across a -10 °C to 50 °C temperature range and withstands ±8 kV air discharge and ±4 kV contact discharge ESD events. At the same time, the units are designed to tolerate continuous vibration, equipment impact, and strong electromagnetic interference—conditions that typically cause touch drift, data corruption, or outright failure in standard computing hardware.

The result is a fanless industrial pc design rated for more than 50,000 hours of operational life, a critical metric for enterprises calculating total cost of ownership (TCO) across multi-year depreciation cycles. Installation flexibility is equally robust, with support for VESA arm, wall-mount, panel-embed, and desktop stand configurations, allowing the same industrial panel pc hardware to adapt from cramped machine-control enclosures to centralized dispatch consoles.

Windows Panel PC and Android Panel PC Options

Arrvel is launching the series with three distinct models—N15L6, A15L6, and K12L2—each targeting different performance tiers, software ecosystems, and price points while sharing the same hardened thermal, mechanical, and electrical architecture.

The N15L6 serves as the workhorse for windows panel pc deployments in industrial automation and MES/ESOP environments. It is powered by the Intel Celeron N5905 processor running Windows 11, with 8 GB of RAM and 128 GB of storage. Under continuous load, Arrvel benchmarks the platform as delivering a 40–60 percent composite performance improvement over the previous-generation N5100, a gain that translates directly to snappier HMI responsiveness and faster data logging on the production line.

For Android-native environments and emerging edge-AI workloads, the A15L6 is Arrvel's flagship android panel pc, adopting the Rockchip RK3576 system-on-chip. Built on an 8 nm process, the RK3576 features eight cores running at up to 2.2 GHz and integrates a dedicated 6 TOPS NPU for on-device inference. Compared to the legacy RK3399, Arrvel cites a 45 percent improvement in single-threaded performance and a 130–140 percent lift in multi-threaded throughput. The unit ships with Android 14, 4 GB of RAM, and 64 GB of storage, and uniquely includes Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, and onboard 4G LTE connectivity as standard—reducing peripheral clutter in mobile kiosk and remote monitoring applications.

At the high-performance tier, the K12L2 stands as Arrvel's high-performance panel pc, upgrading to the Intel Core i5-1235U processor with Windows 11, again paired with 8 GB of RAM and 128 GB of storage. This configuration targets complex machine-vision gateways, multi-protocol industrial data concentrators, and graphics-intensive HMI visualization where multi-threaded processing and rapid I/O throughput are non-negotiable.

Industrial Panel Mount PC Customization and I/O Flexibility

A persistent pain point in industrial digitization is the interface mismatch between modern computing platforms and legacy field equipment. Arrvel addresses this with a densely populated, standard I/O array across the industrial panel mount pc series: dual USB 2.0 Type-A ports, dual USB 3.0 Type-A ports, one HDMI output, one VGA output, one Gigabit RJ45 Ethernet port, dual RS232 serial ports (with COM2 configurable to RS485), dedicated line-in and line-out audio jacks, and a 12 V DC input. The A15L6 additionally includes a USB Type-C port for contemporary peripheral connectivity.

Beyond the baseline configuration, Arrvel offers extensive factory-level customization. Processor options range from low-power Intel platforms (N5095, J1900, J6412) through 4th to 12th generation Intel Core i3, i5, and i7 processors. Memory scales from 4 GB to 64 GB, and storage options span 64 GB eMMC up to 1 TB SSD, with an optional 2.5-inch mechanical hard drive bay for data-logging-intensive applications. Operating system support covers Windows XP through Windows 11 and mainstream Linux distributions, protecting customers with legacy software dependencies.

Display sizes range from 10.1 inches—optimized for embedded machine-control panels—to 21.5 inches for centralized monitoring stations, with ten intermediate sizes available. I/O customization extends to expanding USB port count to four to six, serial ports to six channels (RS232/RS485), and LAN interfaces to four independent Gigabit ports. Power input can be reconfigured to Phoenix terminal blocks for industrial cabinet wiring, and optional modules include 9–36 V wide-voltage power supplies, 1D/2D barcode scanners, NFC readers, dedicated cameras, and GPS receivers.

HMI Panel Applications Across Industrial Scenarios

Arrvel has architected the hmi panel series around four primary verticals where hardware failure carries disproportionate operational and financial consequences.

In manufacturing execution systems (MES) and electronic standard operating procedures (ESOP), the units replace paper-based work instructions and intermittent manual data entry. Deployed at individual workstations, the panel pc devices push real-time work orders, quality benchmarks, and digital SOPs directly to operators. Touch-based task acknowledgment and exception reporting close the manufacturing data loop without the transcription errors and multi-hour latency inherent in paper logs.

For industrial automation and CNC machine interfaces, the fanless sealed architecture prevents metal dust and cutting-fluid mist from penetrating the system, while the wide-temperature rating and EMI hardening maintain signal integrity in electrically noisy environments adjacent to variable frequency drives and high-current switching equipment. The result is a stable hmi panel that does not suffer from touchscreen drift or system lockups during critical machining cycles.

In electrical power monitoring and substation automation, the units function as localized HMI nodes connected directly to protection relays and remote terminal units via serial and Ethernet links. The wide-voltage input tolerance and EMC-compliant design mitigate data jitter and touchscreen drift caused by grid transients and strong magnetic fields, supporting true 7×24 monitoring reliability.

Finally, in unattended commercial self-service and smart healthcare terminals, the strengthened glass and IP65 front panel withstand abrasive cleaning, high-frequency touch interactions, and accidental liquid ingress. The absence of cooling fans eliminates a primary vector for dust accumulation and acoustic noise, supporting continuous operation with reduced preventive maintenance cycles—critical for kiosks and medical check-in terminals where downtime directly impacts revenue and patient throughput.

Closing

The Arrvel panel pc series represents a deliberate engineering response to the hidden costs of deploying consumer-grade computing hardware in industrial environments. By combining passive thermal management, IP65 front-panel protection, wide-voltage and wide-temperature operation, and a modular I/O philosophy across both x86 and ARM architectures, Arrvel offers system integrators and end-users an industrial panel pc platform that is configurable to the application rather than adapted through aftermarket accessories. For organizations seeking a reliable industrial pc partner for next-generation edge deployments, the series is available now through our official online store, Amazon US, and Amazon Germany.

data.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran businessÂ
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027. 

Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.

"After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week.

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture." 

"We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters. 

A spokesperson for the Brooklyn US Attorney's office, which brought the case, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither the White House nor China's embassy in Washington immediately responded to requests for comment on the verdict. 

Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference.

Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence.

FOUNDER'S DAUGHTER WAS DETAINED

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped.

Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC ( HSBC ) banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC ( HSBC ), Standard Chartered ( SCBFF ) and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.

THE PROSECUTION CASE

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu ( FJTSF ) booth at a trade show to photograph a device. 

Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran. 

The defense argued that HSBC ( HSBC ) and the other banks knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for Huawei's business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development." 

The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries. 

(Additional reporting by Luc Cohen and Jonathan Stempel; Editing by Jonathan Spicer, Noeleen Walder and Will Dunham)

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: QHSLab Provides Shareholder Update: Year-to-Date ISP Revenue Grows 64% as Management Prioritizes Sustainable Profitability and Operating Cash Flow
data.description:
Year-to-date revenue increases 13.4%, gross margin improves to 67.9%, and interest expense declines 90%.

West Palm Beach, FL, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- QHSLab, Inc. ( USAQ ) (the “Company”) , an SEC-reporting healthcare technology and software-as-a-service (SaaS) company whose annual financial statements are independently audited, today provided a shareholder update regarding its financial performance for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the continued evolution of its business, and management’s operational and strategic priorities as the Company approaches 2027.

Dear Shareholders,

While much of our communication is shaped by SEC reporting requirements, I wanted to take the time to write to you personally and share my perspective on where we are as a business and where we are heading.

Following the filing of our quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the period ended September 30, 2026, I wanted to provide our shareholders with additional perspective on our financial performance, the continued evolution of our business, and management’s priorities as we approach 2027.

During the first nine months of 2026, we continued to make progress in transitioning QHSLab ( USAQ ) toward a scalable, technology-enabled healthcare services business. While we achieved meaningful growth in our Integrated Service Program (ISP) and improved our gross margins, we also experienced a decline in our allergy diagnostics and immunotherapy business, increased operating expenses and greater demands on our available cash resources.

Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Highlights

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, the Company reported the following unaudited financial results:

  • Total revenue increased 13.4% to $2,253,347, compared with $1,987,931.
  • ISP revenue increased 63.9% to $1,287,692, compared with $785,506.
  • Gross profit increased 15.6% to $1,529,050, compared with $1,322,590.
  • Gross margin improved to 67.9%, compared with 66.5%.
  • Interest expense decreased 90.0% to $19,482, compared with $194,894.
  • Net loss totaled $119,021, compared with a net loss of $99,156.

Continued Growth of Our Integrated Service Program

Our ISP remains the principal driver of revenue growth and an important component of our long-term business strategy.

During the first nine months of 2026, ISP revenue increased by $502,186, representing year-over-year growth of 63.9%. More importantly, ISP now accounts for approximately 57% of our total revenue, compared with approximately 40% during the corresponding period in 2025.

This change in revenue composition reflects the continued evolution of QHSLab ( USAQ ) toward a software-enabled healthcare services business built around ongoing relationships with medical practices.

During the third quarter of 2026, ISP revenue increased 17.4% year-over-year to $421,792. While the rate of growth moderated compared with the first half of the year, the program continued to expand its contribution to our overall business.

We remain focused on acquiring new medical practice customers, increasing utilization among existing customers, expanding our portfolio of digital healthcare services, and improving the operational efficiency and scalability of our service delivery model.

Allergy Diagnostics and Immunotherapy Treatment

Combined revenue from allergy diagnostic kit sales and immunotherapy treatment decreased 19.3% to $828,854 during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $1,027,611 during the corresponding period in 2025.

The decline was more pronounced during the third quarter, with combined allergy-related revenue decreasing 37.0%, reflecting lower purchasing activity among certain existing physician customers. As a result, despite continued ISP revenue growth, total third-quarter revenue decreased 8.1% to $677,172.

In September 2026, we implemented changes to our supplier arrangements that are expected to reduce the cost of our allergy diagnostic kits by approximately 10% to 13%, based on historical sales volumes and product mix. These changes are intended to improve the profitability of future allergy diagnostic kit sales.

Management remains focused on improving the commercial and financial performance of this established business line.

Gross Margins, Operating Expenses and Profitability

Despite the decline in allergy-related revenue, our overall gross margin improved to 67.9% for the first nine months of 2026, compared with 66.5% during the corresponding period in 2025.

For the nine-month period, gross profit increased by $206,460, or 15.6%, compared with the prior year. However, total operating expenses increased by $401,737, or 32.7%, principally reflecting increased personnel, sales and marketing expenditures, corporate insurance and administrative costs.

Research and development expenditures decreased approximately 5% to $350,604, while we continued to enhance our proprietary technology platform and expand our healthcare service capabilities.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into our engineering and software development processes is improving development efficiency, accelerating product enhancements and enabling us to scale our technology platform without a corresponding increase in development expenditures.

We are increasingly realizing the benefits of our historical investments in technology, software architecture and clinical intellectual property. Our existing technology infrastructure and engineering resources are currently sufficient to support our planned platform enhancements, expansion of healthcare service capabilities and growth in customer utilization.

While the full commercial and financial benefits of these developments are not yet reflected in our revenue and earnings, management believes we are establishing a more capital-efficient and scalable business model. Our technology platform is designed to accommodate a substantially larger customer base without requiring proportionate increases in development expenditure.

As we approach 2027, our focus is increasingly shifting toward commercial execution, customer acquisition, utilization and generating financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

We believe this represents an important stage in the evolution of QHSLab ( USAQ ) as we work toward sustainable profitability and positive operating cash flow.

Management recognizes the need to improve operating leverage by generating additional revenue from the technology, personnel and operational infrastructure already established within the business. Our priority is to translate future revenue growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow.

Liquidity and Capital Resources

During the past twelve months, we substantially reduced our outstanding debt obligations and associated financing costs. Interest expense for the first nine months of 2026 declined by approximately $175,000 compared with the corresponding period in 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported:

  • Cash and cash equivalents of $190,464.
  • Net accounts receivable of $308,923.
  • Total current assets of $519,108.
  • Total current liabilities of $247,114.
  • Positive working capital of $271,994.
  • No outstanding long-term liabilities.

Total liabilities decreased approximately 54.7%, from $546,078 at December 31, 2025, to $247,114 at September 30, 2026.

Cash decreased by $445,693 during the first nine months of 2026, reflecting approximately $335,000 used in operating activities and $111,000 used in financing activities related to debt repayment. This compares with approximately $80,000 generated from operating activities during the corresponding period in 2025. Operating cash flow during 2026 was impacted by operating losses, increased accounts receivable and a reduction in outstanding accounts payable.

Management remains focused on improving cash collections, managing operating expenditures and increasing the contribution of ongoing service-based revenues to operating cash flow.

While the reduction in debt has lowered financing costs, improving liquidity remains an important priority. As disclosed in our Form 10-Q, substantial doubt remains regarding the Company's ability to continue as a going concern. Our ability to continue operations depends upon achieving sustainable positive operating cash flow or obtaining additional financing, if necessary.

Our objective remains to increasingly support the business through internally generated cash flow.

Management's Focus as We Approach 2027

As we approach 2027, our operational priorities remain clear:

  • Expand our network of medical practice customers and accelerate customer activation.
  • Increase ongoing service revenue through greater utilization of ISP among new and existing customers.
  • Commercialize additional software-enabled healthcare programs using our existing technology infrastructure.
  • Improve the commercial and financial performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business.
  • Generate greater operating leverage from our existing technology, personnel and administrative infrastructure.
  • Improve cash collections, expenditure management and operating efficiency.
  • Work toward sustainable operating profitability and positive cash flow.

We believe the progress we have made in developing our technology platform, expanding our healthcare service capabilities and reducing our financing costs provides a foundation for the next stage of our business development.

Management Commentary

“Building a sustainable healthcare technology company requires us to remain focused on the fundamentals of our business. We are encouraged by the continued growth of our Integrated Service Program and its increasing contribution to our overall revenue. At the same time, we recognize that revenue growth alone is not enough. We must translate that growth into improved operating profitability and positive cash flow,” said Troy Grogan, President and Chief Executive Officer of QHSLab ( USAQ ).

“Our priorities are to grow revenue, improve the performance of our allergy diagnostics and treatment business, exercise greater discipline over operating expenditures, and generate improved financial returns from the technology and operational infrastructure we have established.

“An important development that may not yet be fully apparent in our financial results is the increasing scalability of our technology and the productivity of our engineering team. We are developing more capabilities, expanding our healthcare service offerings and improving our platform without increasing our research and development expenditures. data.title: Nvidia board's Huang reversal raises doubts about independence, critics say
data.description:
BOSTON/NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board undermined its claims of independence by reinstating CEO Jensen Huang before investigations into his conduct concluded, investors and corporate governance experts said on Monday.

The decision is striking because the board effectively vouched for Huang's candor and fitness to lead the company before its own investigation was complete, raising doubts about whether directors had sufficient information to make an independent judgment, these people said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said on Monday that after talks with senior US officials, its board "is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

Huang resigned on November 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

The abrupt U-turn, just days after the board vowed to look elsewhere for a successor, has also drawn US President Donald Trump and his administration into Nvidia's ( NVDA ) corporate governance. Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares closed 31.5% higher on Monday even as it was becoming clear that the chipmaker's board acted under pressure from Trump and others, and the president took credit for the change.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) faces investigations, including by the US Securities and Exchange Commission and the Justice Department, over issues ranging from its accounting to alleged chip smuggling. Nvidia ( NVDA ) press representatives did not immediately respond to questions for this story.

The situation undercuts the board's standing, said New York City Comptroller Mark Levine, who helps manage retirement funds that hold some 5 million Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"They told us flatly that he would not be coming back. They have done a total 180 without any explanation, or any indication that concerns about legal and other liabilities have been resolved," Levine said in a telephone interview. 

"They have proven they're not independent, and that is the defining quality that we need from any board," he said.

Jan van Eck, a large Nvidia ( NVDA ) investor via the investment company bearing his name, said Huang's return likely removes uncertainty but amounts to a bet against further bad headlines.

"I had expected more of a Washington DC process, including Congressional hearings, to lengthen this determination, but I guess the Administration is willing to risk that there are no more bad facts to emerge," van Eck said in an email.   

QUESTIONS OF CANDOR

In addition to saying Huang's return posed no national security risk, Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board said that after discussions, it was "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA ( NVDA )."  

The company said an independent board committee is still investigating reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and said "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion," with Huang's cooperation. The board has also taken steps like creating a new chief compliance officer position.

Nada Kakabadse, a Henley Business School professor who follows corporate governance, said the statement left gaps. " 'Satisfied with his candor' is a strange phrase while the investigation into what he told the company is still open. The board has reached its verdict before the evidence is in," Kakabadse said. 

Moreover, the board has given away much of the company's room for maneuver, she said. "It hands the board's judgment to the state. The same government that grants Nvidia's ( NVDA ) export licences now effectively vouches for its CEO. That makes the company politically dependent, and a future administration could withdraw the endorsement," she said.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) board member Harvey Jones took the title of chair only this month. Until then, Nvidia ( NVDA ) was one of only two companies in the S&P 500 without a board chair, according to researcher Equilar. 

Corporate governance experts previously had said the setup and the presence of many long-serving directors meant the board would have to show it could act independently.  

Now, alongside relief at Huang's return, "there are sure to be questions about who is best placed to provide appropriate governance and oversight of key risks at the now-giant company at the center of a critically important global AI ecosystem," said Lindsey Stewart, Morningstar director of institutional insights. In reappointing Huang the board left those questions unanswered, Stewart said.

SKEPTICISM FROM SOME LAWMAKERS

US congressional committees will interview Huang on December 1. Lawmakers from both parties expressed skepticism about his return and the role of the administration. Some investors worried the political battles could overshadow Nvidia's ( NVDA ) commercial story.

"Jensen's return is not a total shock, but it does send a troubling message about the state of corporate governance in America. Certain executives are going to be held to different standards," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer of Ocean Park Asset Management in California.  

Harvard Law School Professor Lucian Bebchuk said there was no indication the board had secured the support of Nvidia's largest shareholders, nominally the owners of the company. (Top fund firms BlackRock and Vanguard did not comment for this story.) 

Bebchuk said recent policies put in place by Trump-appointed regulators make it harder for big fund firms to weigh in on corporate governance issues.

Even if Huang poses no national security risks in the future, his actions to date could still entangle him and the company in costly investigations, Bebchuk said.

"The board presumably feels now vindicated by the immediate stock price increase following this morning's announcement. However, the board's reversal of its earlier decision raises serious questions and concerns," Bebchuk said.     

(Reporting by Ross Kerber in Boston and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Toby Sterling in Amsterdam and Chibuike Oguh in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

The computer maker reported its latest financial results late Tuesday. Revenue in the personal systems division, HP's computer business, climbed 14% year over year to $11.75 billion for the quarter ended October.

HP increased its AI PC penetration to nearly 60% of shipments in the quarter, "well ahead" of its 50% target, Chief Financial Officer Karen Parkhill said during an earnings conference call, according to a FactSet transcript. The company saw continued demand for its AI PCs, interim Chief Executive Bruce Broussard said on the call.

Continued AI PC adoption and stable demand from enterprise customers are likely to support growth in the personal systems segment, RBC said in a client note emailed Friday.

However, the brokerage said it remains "cautious" about margin pressures in the personal systems business stemming from higher memory prices and rising input costs. RBC also highlighted the potential for "demand destruction" in the PC market due to higher average selling prices.

The brokerage has a sector perform rating on the stock with a price target of $33.

HP expects its personal systems operating margin to improve sequentially in fiscal 2027, Parkhill told analysts on the call. The metric fell to 3% in the fiscal fourth quarter from 5.8% a year earlier.

"Given the challenging environment in consumer, we proactively took pricing adjustments to address channel health in the quarter, which resulted in a margin below our initial expectation," Parkhill said.

The company is taking measures to improve its margin, such as designs with lower costs and competitive sourcing to generate sequential improvement through the next year, the CFO added.

For the fiscal fourth quarter, HP reported adjusted earnings of $0.83 per share, down from $0.93 a year earlier, while overall revenue advanced 9.3% to $16 billion. data.title: Court To Overturn Marijuana Rescheduling Order? MMJ Citing Immediate And Irreparable Economic Harm
data.description:
WASHINGTON, D.C. / ACCESS Newswire / November 25, 2026 / MMJ International Holdings, Inc. ("MMJIH"), together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc. (collectively, "MMJ"), and a coalition of injured parties, filed their opening brief yesterday in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit seeking to hold unlawful and set aside Attorney General Order No. 6754-2026 rescheduling marijuana.

The litigation challenges the legality of the April 28, 2026 Order, which established a separate federal regulatory pathway for state-licensed medical marijuana businesses while companies pursuing the established federal pharmaceutical development pathway remain subject to extensive FDA and DEA requirements.

MMJ occupies a distinct position among the petitioners: it is a commercial pharmaceutical developer alleging direct and continuing economic injury resulting from the Order.

THE ECONOMIC DAMAGE IS HAPPENING NOW

"MMJ is not hurt by what this Order might do someday. We are hurt by what it is doing right now," stated Duane Boise, President and Chief Executive Officer of MMJ International Holdings.

"For eight years and more than $10 million, MMJ has pursued the federal regulatory pathway to develop pharmaceutical medicines from marijuana. We filed our FDA Investigational New Drug applications, secured an Orphan Drug Designation, established a DEA-registered Schedule I analytical laboratory and manufactured a finished pharmaceutical soft-gel capsule.

"That investment in federal compliance was supposed to be our competitive advantage. Instead, the government has turned it into a competitive disadvantage."

State marijuana operators are already receiving DEA registrations, while certain publicly traded operators have announced that they are no longer applying the federal tax restrictions imposed by Section 280E.

Meanwhile, thousands of state operators have applied for federal registrations under a framework that permits qualifying timely applicants to continue operating while their applications remain pending.

"Our competitors are already realizing regulatory and economic benefits while MMJ continues to wait for its federal bulk-manufacturer registration," Boise continued.

"Investors are already questioning why the federal government has extended these benefits to businesses that bypassed federal requirements. Every day this Order remains in effect, MMJ's competitive position, investment value and pharmaceutical market opportunity are being eroded. A later court ruling cannot necessarily restore what has already been lost."

THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT IS PENALIZING COMPLIANCE

MMJ has invested more than eight years and $10 million in scientific research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, analytical testing, regulatory submissions and clinical development.

Its regulatory and pharmaceutical milestones include:

  • Two FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) applications targeting Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis.
  • FDA Orphan Drug Designation for its Huntington's disease drug development program.
  • A DEA Schedule I analytical laboratory registration and Rhode Island laboratory license CAL00016.
  • Manufacturing of 50,000 pharmaceutical-grade THC/CBD soft-gel capsules under Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
  • Rhode Island cultivation/manufacturing licensure .
  • A pending DEA bulk-manufacturer application originally submitted in December 2018.

While MMJ has invested in standardized formulations, pharmaceutical manufacturing, stability testing and regulatory compliance, state dispensaries are already selling cannabinoid capsules, tablets and other products marketed for therapeutic purposes without those products necessarily undergoing equivalent FDA drug-development review.

MMJ contends that the Order creates an unequal competitive environment that undermines the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, effective and scientifically validated cannabinoid medicines.

FIVE FUNDAMENTAL LEGAL CHALLENGES TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S ORDER

The petitioners' opening brief challenges the Order on multiple statutory and administrative-law grounds, arguing that it:

  1. Violates the Controlled Substances Act by assigning marijuana to different schedules based on state licensing status rather than the statutory scheduling criteria.
  2. Bypasses required federal rulemaking procedures under 21 U.S.C. § 811, raising issues addressed by the D.C. Circuit in NORML v. DEA (1977), as well as questions concerning the scope of the Attorney General's statutory authority.
  3. Conflicts with international drug treaty obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs of 1961, including requirements governing cultivation, production quotas, government oversight, crop possession, distribution and medical prescriptions.
  4. Rewrites federal controlled-substance regulations without required notice-and-comment rulemaking, establishing alternative regulatory requirements for state marijuana businesses.
  5. Reverses previous federal regulatory positions without adequate explanation, including concerns previously identified by DEA regarding diversion, public safety and inconsistent regulatory standards across state marijuana programs.

These challenges raise fundamental questions about whether the Attorney General possessed the statutory authority to establish an alternative federal regulatory system for an existing state marijuana industry.

DEA'S OWN FINDINGS RAISE QUESTIONS ABOUT STATE REGULATORY SAFEGUARDS

The Attorney General's Order asserts that state medical marijuana regulatory systems have developed robust infrastructure for preventing diversion, ensuring product safety, maintaining records and conducting facility inspections.

Yet DEA's own 2025 National Drug Threat Assessment documents marijuana trafficking from states where marijuana is legal under state law into other jurisdictions and identifies vulnerabilities exploited by criminal organizations.

Additionally, recent litigation brought by state marijuana operators themselves has highlighted the difficulties of reconciling existing state marijuana supply chains with federal controlled-substance requirements and international treaty obligations.

MMJ believes these developments raise serious questions about the factual and legal foundations of the Attorney General's Order.

"The issue has never been whether marijuana has therapeutic potential," Boise stated. "The issue is whether the federal government can abandon established regulatory safeguards, reward businesses that historically operated outside federal law and economically injure companies that followed the law."

INTERNATIONAL DRUG TREATY OBLIGATIONS ARE NOT OPTIONAL

MMJ maintains that the United States cannot disregard its obligations under the Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs simply to accommodate an established commercial marijuana industry.

Federal oversight of marijuana cultivation, production quotas, inventory, distribution and medical use raises significant legal questions that cannot be resolved merely by recognizing existing state licenses.

MMJ's pharmaceutical development program has been structured around established federal controls governing controlled substances intended for medical and scientific purposes.

"MMJ built its business around federal law. The state marijuana industry built its business around state law despite federal prohibition. Now the federal government is attempting to reconcile those two fundamentally different systems at the expense of companies that complied with federal requirements," Boise said.

MMJ SEEKS SWIFT JUDICIAL RELIEF

MMJ joins the States of Nebraska and Indiana, Smart Approaches to Marijuana (SAM), the National Drug and Alcohol Screening Association (NDASA), New Directions Addiction Recovery Services, Cannabis Industry Victims Educating Litigators (CIVEL), and Drs. Kenneth Finn and Elizabeth Stuyt in challenging the Attorney General's Order.

MMJ is represented by Burke Law Group, PLLC.

The company hopes the D.C. Circuit will swiftly remedy its injury, as MMJ continues to suffer economic and competitive harm for as long as the Order remains in effect.

"This is not a fight against marijuana rescheduling. It is a fight against unlawful rescheduling, unequal regulatory treatment and the destruction of the economic incentives necessary to develop safe, scientifically validated pharmaceutical medicines," Boise concluded.

"Federal compliance should be rewarded - not punished."

About MMJ International Holdings

MMJ International Holdings, Inc., together with its subsidiaries MMJ BioPharma Cultivation, Inc. and MMJ BioPharma Labs, Inc., based in Westerly, Rhode Island, is a pharmaceutical development company focused on standardized cannabinoid medicines derived from natural marijuana extracts through established FDA and DEA regulatory pathways.

Its clinical development programs target serious neurological conditions, including Huntington's disease and multiple sclerosis, using GMP-manufactured THC/CBD soft-gel capsules designed for clinical trials.

data.title: Economic Growth Rose Slightly to Moderately in Most Fed Districts, Beige Book Shows
data.description:
02:26 PM EST, 11/25/2026 (MT Newswires) -- There was only slight to moderate growth in eight of the 12 Federal Reserve districts, with no change in the other four districts, the Federal Reserve's most recent Beige Book update released Wednesday showed.

"Consumer spending was little changed, as households remained price sensitive and were increasingly selective in discretionary purchases," according to the Beige Book summary, also noting softer auto sales due to higher fuel prices and interest rates.

Manufacturing activity was up modestly, but residential real estate activity weakened due to affordability challenges, the summary showed.

"Port volumes were slightly lower due to weather-driven disruptions, even as data center-related imports rose," the summary said. "Energy activity grew modestly but investment in this sector remained restrained by elevated geopolitical, policy, and cost uncertainties."

Employment levels were up only slightly, with firms noting stable payroll and hiring only to replace departing workers.

"Contacts across several sectors cited steady or rising labor demand, though many also described hesitancy to hire amid uncertainty and weakened consumer spending," the summary showed. "Labor supply generally remained stable, and while it was often relatively easy to find workers, persistent hiring difficulties continued for skilled and technical roles."

Wages and benefits were up moderately compared with only modest growth in the previous Beige Book report, with more growth in sectors where positions were hard to fill.

"Prices increased moderately overall, as in the prior reporting period," according to the summary. "Contacts across a range of sectors reported sustained cost pressure from energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance, and tariff-related expenses."

Further increases in both expenses and prices are expected in the coming month, the Beige Book said.

Scottsdale, AZ, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Mortgage lenders evaluating the best mortgage live transfer providers in the United States are increasingly prioritizing application conversion rates, funded-loan acquisition costs and loan officer productivity over traditional lead volume and per-lead pricing.

Radian Leads, a nationwide mortgage live transfer provider founded in 2025, is highlighting its fourth-quarter performance benchmarks as lenders reassess the economics of mortgage borrower acquisition and the performance of their lead generation partners.

The company's previously published performance data includes a 19.6% overall transfer-to-application conversion rate, with individual cash-out refinance campaigns achieving application conversion rates of up to 41.7%.

What defines the highest-performing mortgage live transfer providers?

While traditional mortgage lead generation companies have historically emphasized lead volume, Radian Leads measures performance through borrower engagement, completed applications and estimated funded-loan acquisition costs.

The company's published mortgage live transfer performance metrics include:

  • 41.7% first-call application conversion on a cash-out refinance campaign.
  • 19.6% overall mortgage live transfer application conversion.
  • 83.3% of billable transfers progressing to identity or credit intake on the cash-out refinance campaign.
  • 100% of billable transfers on that campaign involving homeowners seeking to access home equity.
  • 23 minutes and 39 seconds of average loan officer engagement per billable transfer on that campaign.
  • 34 minutes and 24 seconds of average conversation time on calls resulting in completed applications.

These performance indicators provide mortgage executives with a framework for evaluating the highest-converting mortgage leads and comparing live transfer lead generation companies based on measurable business outcomes.

Mortgage borrower acquisition costs and campaign economics

Radian Leads estimates funded-loan acquisition costs ranging from approximately $530 to $1,221, using a 50% application-to-funding conversion baseline across its modeled acquisition scenarios.

At the company's reported 41.7% campaign application conversion rate, approximately 2.4 billable mortgage live transfers are required to generate one completed mortgage application.

Across its broader mortgage live transfer portfolio, Radian Leads has also reported estimated funded-loan acquisition costs ranging from $802 to $864, based on application-to-funding assumptions of 65% to 70%.

These estimates illustrate why mortgage lenders evaluating the best mortgage lead generation companies may benefit from measuring acquisition costs at the application and funded-loan level rather than exclusively comparing the purchase price of individual leads or live transfers.

Actual funded-loan acquisition costs depend on campaign performance, lending criteria and lender-specific funding conversion rates.

Exclusive mortgage live transfers for residential mortgage lenders

Radian Leads delivers exclusive, pre-screened mortgage live transfers directly to mortgage lenders, brokers, credit unions and licensed loan officers across the United States.

The company's mortgage live transfer programs include:

  • VA cash-out refinance live transfers
  • FHA cash-out refinance live transfers
  • Conventional cash-out refinance live transfers
  • HELOC live transfers
  • Home equity loan live transfers
  • Mortgage refinance live transfers
  • Purchase mortgage live transfers
  • Reverse mortgage live transfers

Borrowers are screened against lender-specific qualification requirements, geographic licensing restrictions, mortgage product eligibility and campaign delivery criteria before being connected with a lending professional.

Radian Leads operates its own telecommunications, call routing, recording, transcription and quality assurance infrastructure, providing mortgage lenders with visibility into individual borrower interactions and campaign-level conversion performance.

Establishing a higher standard for mortgage lead generation

For mortgage lenders determining which companies provide the best mortgage live transfers, Radian Leads emphasizes five core performance indicators: borrower qualification, exclusivity, application conversion, loan officer engagement and funded-loan acquisition costs.

The company's published results support its broader objective of establishing higher performance standards within the mortgage live transfer industry and improving the economics of residential mortgage borrower acquisition.

Radian Leads continues to provide lender-facing resources and performance data covering mortgage lead generation, live transfer conversion rates, borrower qualification and customer acquisition economics.

Additional information about Radian Leads and its mortgage live transfer programs is available at https://www.radianleads.com.

About Radian Leads

Founded in 2025, Radian Leads is a nationwide mortgage live transfer provider specializing in exclusive borrower acquisition for mortgage lenders, brokers and credit unions. The company delivers pre-screened mortgage live transfers across VA, FHA, conventional, HELOC, home equity and other residential lending programs. Radian Leads operates its own telecommunications, call routing, recording and quality assurance infrastructure. Its mission is to establish higher standards for mortgage borrower acquisition through measurable conversion performance, operational transparency and efficient funded-loan acquisition.

data.title: SEDA Strengthens Its Capital Markets and Financing Instruments Practices with the Addition of Brendan Scarf
data.description:
New York, NY, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SEDA Experts LLC, a leading expert witness firm providing world-class financial expert witness services, announced today that Brendan Scarf joined the firm as Managing Director.

“We are delighted to welcome Brendan to SEDA Experts. He has extensive experience in Structured Finance and Private Credit globally which will be of great value to our clients,” said Rakesh Manani, Partner - Head of Asia Pacific of SEDA Experts.

Brendan Scarf is a structured finance, private credit, and capital markets expert with 21 years of experience originating, structuring, and executing complex transactions across the United States, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. He is recognised for his ability to identify and structure bespoke financing solutions in sophisticated and often highly complex situations, combining deep technical expertise with extensive experience across credit, equity, securitisation, and alternative investment markets.

Mr. Scarf spent eight years at Deutsche Bank AG, where he ultimately served as Head of Global Markets Structuring for Australia and New Zealand. In that role, he led the bank's most complex structured transactions, advising on acquisition financings, structured credit investments, securitisation platforms, distressed portfolio acquisitions, and institutional capital solutions. His work included several landmark transactions involving large financial institutions, private equity sponsors, and alternative investment managers, as well as the development of innovative financing and risk-management structures across multiple asset classes.

Prior to joining Deutsche Bank AG, he held a number of increasingly senior roles at Macquarie Bank Limited across Sydney, London, and New York. He originated and executed financing transactions for hedge funds, private equity investors, institutional asset managers, and other sophisticated market participants. His experience encompassed structured lending, leverage facilities, portfolio financing, equity-linked products, and alternative investment strategies, while also contributing to the design and commercialisation of new investment and financing platforms.

Following his time at Deutsche Bank AG he was the Founder, Director, and Portfolio Manager of Carrara Capital, where he managed investments across private and public market structured finance opportunities. Mr. Scarf continues to work at the intersection of structuring, investment management, and private credit. As Head of Structuring at Human Financial, he has been involved in the acquisition and development of substantial investment platforms and trading capabilities.

Throughout his career, he has developed extensive expertise in structured finance, securitisation, acquisition finance, institutional lending, private credit, structured equity, portfolio management, and complex capital solutions. He is a Chartered Financial Analyst and an ASX Accredited Derivatives Advisor. He holds degrees in Commerce and Civil Engineering from the University of Sydney.

About SEDA Experts LLC

SEDA is a leading expert witness firm specializing in financial services. We support international law firms by offering the highest level of expertise across the financial industry and providing access to the most influential financial services industry leaders. We provide superior independent advice, data analytics, valuation, and high-quality expert reports and testimony services to law firms, regulators, and leading financial institutions.
